subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron output target contract that can write files, fan out to channels, and inject session context, or should cron keep the current delivery modes and solve narrower routing failures separately?
rationale: This changes public cron config and creates scheduler-owned file, channel, and session side effects, so automation cannot safely choose the API, authorization, fallback, and audit semantics.

options.title: Design one output contract
options.body: Approve a single cron output-routing design covering file, channel, session, fallback, run-status, docs, and security boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Keep narrower delivery issues
options.body: Leave this umbrella open only as design context and address defaults, topic routing, and file-save bugs through narrower existing issues.

options.title: Decline framework-owned targets
options.body: Keep cron output routing prompt/tool-owned and close the feature direction if scheduler-owned side effects are not desired.

recommendation.title: Design one output contract
recommendation.body: Approve a single cron output-routing design covering file, channel, session, fallback, run-status, docs, and security boundaries before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product/security-sensitive, and this handle appears as committer on the original delivery-mode change plus recent cron delivery history.
